story: E005-F004-S001: Create actor service for cross-provider hook management
story_description: As a Blaze developer, I need an actor-based service that manages hook configurations across multiple agentic CLI providers (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI) so that hooks can be loaded, saved, merged, and resolved correctly for each provider context.
task_description: Implement the four core methods of MultiProviderHooksService: resolveConfigPath for provider-specific paths, loadHooks for async configuration loading, saveHooks for persisting configurations, and getEffectiveHooks for resolving merged configurations.
atom_description: Create the MultiProviderHooksService actor in Blaze/Sources/Engine/MultiProviderHooksService.swift with Swift actor isolation, implementing resolveConfigPath, loadHooks, saveHooks, and getEffectiveHooks methods that handle provider-specific hook configuration management with proper error handling and thread safety.
problem_statement: Blaze currently lacks a centralized service to manage hook configurations across multiple CLI providers. Each provider stores hooks in different paths and formats (Claude uses .claude/settings.json, Gemini uses .gemini/settings.json, Codex uses .codex/config.toml). Without a unified service, the UI cannot load, display, edit, or save hooks for different providers, and there is no way to merge project-level hooks with worktree-specific overrides.
scope_in: Swift actor definition with proper isolation semantics
resolveConfigPath method returning provider-specific config URL based on provider enum, scope enum, and optional worktree ID
loadHooks async throwing method that reads and parses provider-specific config files into unified HookConfiguration model
saveHooks async throwing method that writes HookConfiguration back to provider-specific format and path
getEffectiveHooks method that merges global, project, and worktree hooks in correct precedence order
Error enum for service-specific failures (fileNotFound, parseError, writeError, invalidProvider)
Integration with existing HookConfiguration and HookNode models from H001-MODELS
Support for all three providers: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI
scope_out: UI components for displaying or editing hooks (handled in H005-UIPROVIDER)
Hook migration between providers (handled in H007-MIGRATE)
Export and installation logic (handled in H008-EXPORT)
TOML parsing for Codex config files (separate utility dependency)
assumptions: HookProvider enum exists from H001-MODELS with cases for claude, gemini, codex
HookScope enum exists with cases for global, project, worktree
HookConfiguration struct exists with hooks dictionary mapping event types to hook entries
Project paths are accessible via existing ProjectManager or passed as parameters
FileManager is available for file operations
Swift actors provide sufficient concurrency safety without additional locking
JSON parsing uses Codable for Claude and Gemini configs
TOML parsing dependency is available for Codex config files
constraints: Must use Swift actor isolation to prevent data races in concurrent access
Config file paths must follow each CLI's documented conventions exactly
loadHooks must not block the main thread
saveHooks must create parent directories if they do not exist
getEffectiveHooks must apply correct precedence: worktree > project > global
Error handling must preserve original error context for debugging
File operations must handle permission errors gracefully
Service must be testable with mock file systems
functional_requirements: FR1: resolveConfigPath(provider:scope:worktreeId:) returns correct URL for each provider/scope combination - Claude: .claude/settings.json, Gemini: .gemini/settings.json, Codex: .codex/config.toml
FR2: loadHooks(provider:scope:worktreeId:) reads config file at resolved path and returns parsed HookConfiguration or throws descriptive error
FR3: saveHooks(_:provider:scope:worktreeId:) serializes HookConfiguration to provider-specific format and writes to resolved path with atomic write
FR4: getEffectiveHooks(provider:worktreeContext:) loads global, project, and optionally worktree hooks and merges them with correct precedence
FR5: Service exposes HooksServiceError enum with cases fileNotFound(URL), parseError(URL, Error), writeError(URL, Error), unsupportedProvider(HookProvider)
FR6: loadHooks returns empty HookConfiguration (not error) when config file does not exist (first-time setup case)
FR7: saveHooks creates parent directories (.claude/, .gemini/, .codex/) if they do not exist before writing
FR8: All async methods support task cancellation via Swift cooperative cancellation
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: loadHooks completes within 100ms for typical config files under 100KB
NFR2: saveHooks performs atomic write to prevent partial file corruption on crash
NFR3: Actor reentrancy must not cause data inconsistency
NFR4: Memory usage for loaded configurations must not exceed 10MB per provider
NFR5: Service must be instantiable as singleton via dependency injection container
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create file Blaze/Sources/Engine/MultiProviderHooksService.swift with actor declaration and HooksServiceError enum
Step 2: Implement resolveConfigPath method with switch on HookProvider and HookScope to construct correct file URLs using project path base
Step 3: Implement loadHooks method with async file read using FileManager, dispatch to JSON or TOML parser based on provider, map to HookConfiguration or throw parseError
Step 4: Implement saveHooks method with directory creation, serialization to provider format, and atomic write via temporary file and rename
Step 5: Implement getEffectiveHooks method that calls loadHooks for each applicable scope and merges configurations using HookConfiguration.merged(with:) method
Step 6: Add extension on HookConfiguration for merged(with:) that combines hooks arrays per event type with later entries taking precedence
Step 7: Add unit tests in Tests/EngineTests/MultiProviderHooksServiceTests.swift with mock file system
Step 8: Add integration test that creates actual config files in temp directory and verifies round-trip load/save
data_model_changes: Add merged(with:) method to HookConfiguration struct for combining two configurations with precedence
Add HooksServiceError enum with fileNotFound, parseError, writeError, unsupportedProvider cases
No schema changes to existing HookConfiguration or HookNode models
api_contracts: MultiProviderHooksService.resolveConfigPath(provider: HookProvider, scope: HookScope, worktreeId: UUID?) -> URL - Returns file URL for hook config based on provider and scope
MultiProviderHooksService.loadHooks(provider: HookProvider, scope: HookScope, worktreeId: UUID?) async throws -> HookConfiguration - Loads and parses hook config from resolved path

MultiProviderHooksService.saveHooks(_ config: HookConfiguration, provider: HookProvider, scope: HookScope, worktreeId: UUID?, projectPath: URL) async throws - Persists hook config to provider-specific format
MultiProviderHooksService.getEffectiveHooks(provider: HookProvider, worktreeContext: WorktreeContext?) async throws -> HookConfiguration - Returns merged hooks with correct precedence
event_contracts: N/A - This service does not emit events; it is called by other components that may emit events
ui_states: N/A - This is a backend service with no direct UI states
ui_interactions: N/A - This is a backend service; UI interactions are handled by H005-UIPROVIDER which consumes this service
ui_copy: N/A - No user-facing copy in this service layer
edge_cases: Edge case 1: Config file exists but is empty - return HookConfiguration with empty hooks dictionary
Edge case 2: Config file has valid JSON but wrong schema - throw parseError with descriptive message including expected vs actual structure
Edge case 3: Config file path has spaces or special characters - URL must handle encoding correctly
Edge case 4: Worktree ID provided but worktree directory no longer exists - throw fileNotFound with worktree context in error
Edge case 5: Concurrent loadHooks and saveHooks for same provider - actor isolation ensures serialization
Edge case 6: saveHooks called while another process holds file lock - retry with exponential backoff up to 3 times then throw writeError
Edge case 7: Config file is symlink - follow symlink and operate on target file
Edge case 8: Global scope path differs per OS (macOS vs future Linux) - use appropriate path resolution
Edge case 9: Codex TOML config has nested tables not supported by basic TOML parser - throw parseError with suggestion to simplify config
failure_modes: File system permission denied on read - throw HooksServiceError.fileNotFound with permission context in description
File system permission denied on write - throw HooksServiceError.writeError with permission context
JSON parse failure - throw HooksServiceError.parseError with line number if available from decoder
TOML parse failure - throw HooksServiceError.parseError with TOML-specific error message
Directory creation failure - throw HooksServiceError.writeError with parent directory path
Disk full during atomic write - throw HooksServiceError.writeError and ensure temp file is cleaned up
Task cancelled during async operation - throw CancellationError without leaving partial state
rollback_plan: If MultiProviderHooksService causes issues: 1) Revert the file addition, 2) Remove any references added to existing files, 3) The hooks builder can fall back to direct file operations as before. No persistent state changes are made by this service that would require data migration on rollback.

risks: Actor reentrancy could cause unexpected behavior if methods call each other
TOML parsing library may have bugs or performance issues with complex configs
File locking race condition with external CLI processes modifying config
Config schema changes in future CLI versions could break parsing
mitigations: Use nonisolated helpers for pure functions to avoid reentrancy
Add comprehensive TOML parsing tests and consider fallback to raw string preservation
Implement file change detection and reload mechanism in future iteration
Use permissive parsing that preserves unknown keys for forward compatibility
risk_register.blast_radius: Failure in this service would prevent hooks from loading or saving in the UI, but would not affect CLI execution since CLIs read their own config files directly. Users could still edit config files manually.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If service has critical bugs, revert to direct file operations in HooksBuilderView as temporary workaround while fix is developed.
